info.name: HS Notify API — BMS / PAS Integration
info.description:
Endpoints for BMS and PAS to trigger notifications directly. Import this collection into Postman, set the `baseUrl` and `apiKey` collection variables, and run requests as-is against the two seeded test rules, or point `ruleCode` at your own rule once it's configured (see notes on each request).

Authentication — two different headers depending on the call:
- Send calls under /api/v1/notifications/** and /api/v1/notify require the `X-HS-API-Key` header. It is set once at the collection level below — do not repeat it per request.
- The two action-discovery GETs (`/api/v1/actions`, `/api/v1/actions/{code}/schema`) are machine lookups with no tenant context, so they authenticate with a separate `X-HS-Lookup-Token` header instead (same pattern as `/api/v1/templates/active` and `/api/v1/rules/active`) — set per-request below, not at the collection level, since it's a different credential.

Before BMS/PAS can successfully call send-by-rule for a given rule:
1. The rule must exist and be status=ACTIVE (created via Notification Rules UI, then approved by a *different* user than the creator — maker-checker).
2. Recipients: **To is dynamic, CC is fixed.** Pass the currently logged-in user's email as `recipientOverride` on every call — that becomes the To address for that send. CC always comes from the rule's configured recipient group and cannot be set by the caller; both PR_CLOSE_RULE and CASE_ESCALATE_RULE are configured to CC `FMS_Group@subex.com` on every send. If `recipientOverride` is omitted, To falls back to `FMS_Group@subex.com` too — so nothing is lost, but you should always send it in real usage.
3. Any `context` keys you send must be on the template's allowed-variables whitelist, or they'll be silently stripped by DLP masking/whitelisting.

variable.description: Shared secret for the unauthenticated action-discovery GETs (X-HS-Lookup-Token header) — separate credential from apiKey, matches hs-notification.security.lookup-token in application.yml.
Set this to whichever user is actually logged into BMS/PAS at call time — it becomes the To address via recipientOverride.

request.description: Confirm the platform is reachable and its DB/mail dependencies are UP before running anything else.

The action picker for the unified /api/v1/notify flow — returns every enabled notification_action (FRAUD_ALERT, ZERO_TOLERANCE, VENDOR_EMAIL, CASE_SUMMARY, PR_CLOSE, DIRECT_SEND) in display_order, each with its `code` (use this as the `action` field on the /notify call) and, if set, a `formSchemaId` telling you whether 'Get Action Schema' below will return anything. Authenticates via `X-HS-Lookup-Token`, not `X-HS-API-Key` — this is a no-tenant-context machine lookup, same pattern as templates/active and rules/active.

Once an action code is picked from 'List Notification Actions', fetch its dynamic form here to render the actual fields — for FRAUD_ALERT this includes to/cc/bcc address, subject, priority + severity dropdowns, a free-text message, two real checkboxes (`include_case_details`, `include_pr_records`), and a recipient-group dynamic lookup. Swap `FRAUD_ALERT` in the path for any other action code from the list call — `schema` comes back `null` (still 200) for actions with no form_schema_id linked yet, e.g. ZERO_TOLERANCE/VENDOR_EMAIL/CASE_SUMMARY today. Same `X-HS-Lookup-Token` auth as the list call above.

item.name: Send By Rule — BMS example (PR closure)

request.description: BMS calls this when a PR closes. `ruleCode` must be an ACTIVE rule (PR_CLOSE_RULE is pre-seeded). `idempotencyKey` must be unique per real-world event — if BMS retries the same call (e.g. on a network timeout) with the same key, the platform returns the original job instead of sending a duplicate email. `recipientOverride` should be set to whichever user is logged into BMS right now — that's who gets the To. CC is always `FMS_Group@subex.com`, fixed on the rule. `context` keys must match the template's variable whitelist (`pr_id`, `account_name`, `closed_by`, `close_date` for PR_CLOSE_MAIL).

item.name: Send By Rule — PAS example (case escalation)

request.description: PAS calls this on a case escalation event. CASE_ESCALATE_RULE must be ACTIVE (approve it from Notification Rules if it's showing DISABLED/PENDING_REVIEW), or this fails with a 'rule not ACTIVE' error. Same recipient pattern as PR_CLOSE_RULE: `recipientOverride` = whoever's logged into PAS, CC is fixed to `FMS_Group@subex.com`.

Use only if BMS/PAS needs to send an ad-hoc email outside the governed rule/approval flow. Recipients are supplied directly in the request rather than pre-configured — no maker-checker, no retry/escalation policy. Prefer send-by-rule for anything recurring.
